Sky Sports News reported Carrick and Fernandes held clear-the-air talks on Tuesday. messages.text: McDermott: England face 'unique task' to progress and can't get distracted

metadata.summary: Brian McDermott has warned his England side not to chase the points as they look to keep their slim Rugby League World Cup hopes alive with a big win against Papua New Guinea.
metadata.content: Rugby League World Cup: England's Brian McDermott admits side face 'unique task' to progress and can't get distracted | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Rugby League World Cup: England's Brian McDermott admits side face 'unique task' to progress and can't get distracted England head coach Brian McDermott speaks to the media on Thursday, as his side seek to avoid historic Rugby League World Cup pool stage exit; England face Papua New Guinea in their final pool fixture on Friday (9.05am kick-off), knowing they need a big win to keep semi-final hopes alive Thursday 29 October 2026 11:13, UK Image: England head coach Brian McDermott spoke to media on Thursday as his side seek to avoid a historic first World Cup pool-stage exit Brian McDermott has warned his England side not to chase the points as they look to keep their slim Rugby League World Cup hopes alive with a big win against Papua New Guinea. England are up against it in their bid to make it through to the semi-finals after they lost 30-12 to Tonga in their opening game. They must beat Papua New Guinea in their final pool game in Woollongong on Friday and then wait until Sunday, when they need Tonga to beat Samoa, upon whom England must also make up a 68-point deficit. That means tries will be the order of the day against Papua New Guinea but McDermott, who saw his side beat France 82-0 in their second game , has called for patience. messages.text: Osaka stunned by 18-year-old Pohankova at Pan Pacific Open in Japan

metadata.summary: Naomi Osaka, seeded No 7 and playing before home fans in Japan, was knocked out of the Pan Pacific Open on Thursday by teenager Mia Pohankova.
metadata.content: Pan Pacific Open: Naomi Osaka stunned by 18-year-old Mia Pohankova and knocked out in front of home crowd in Tokyo | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Pan Pacific Open: Naomi Osaka stunned by 18-year-old Mia Pohankova and knocked out in front of home crowd in Tokyo Japan's Naomi Osaka stunned in front of home crowd as she is knocked out by Slovakian teenager Mia Pohankova in Tokyo exit; You can watch the WTA Pan Pacific Open, WTA Guangzhou Open, ATP Swiss Indoors and ATP Vienna Open live on Sky Sports Tennis Thursday 29 October 2026 08:23, UK Image: Japan's former world No. 1 Naomi Osaka was stunned in Tokyo as she lost to Slovakian teenager Mia Pohankova Naomi Osaka, seeded No 7 and playing before home fans in Japan, was knocked out of the Pan Pacific Open on Thursday by teenager Mia Pohankova. Slovakia's Pohankova, who turned 18 a week ago and was a wild-card entry in Japan, upset Osaka 6-3 7-5 to advance to the quarter-finals. Pohankova will face Alycia Parks in the last eight. Pohankova, the 2025 junior singles champion at Wimbledon, stunned Osaka, who was coming off a win over Jasmine Paolini in the first round in Tokyo. metadata.summary: By the time Saturday rolls around, it will have been 616 days since Tottenham last won three Premier League games on the bounce. Three different managers have come and gone since the feat was last achieved, none able to steer Spurs to a streak of more than two.
metadata.content: Tottenham vs Crystal Palace: Have Spurs genuinely turned a corner in the Premier League under Roberto De Zerbi? | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Tottenham vs Crystal Palace: Have Spurs genuinely turned a corner in the Premier League under Roberto De Zerbi? Three different managers have come and gone since the feat was last achieved, none able to steer Spurs to a streak of more than two. Roberto De Zerbi is the latest boss to try his hand at the hat-trick. Wins over Coventry City and Chelsea have preceded this weekend's meeting with Crystal Palace, live on Sky Sports . The elusive treble is within reach. To right such a wrong would be a huge stepping stone for Spurs under De Zerbi. Not only would the result propel them into the top half of the table, but its potential to heal the wounded Spurs psyche would surely be invaluable.
